summary: Safe degradation policy request: guidance for quant/profile + batching + KV cache fallbacks
description: Issue summary: LexiChat reports increased 95th-percentile tail latency and sporadic streaming disconnects after enabling a new quantization profile and aggressive batching + KV prefetch on their Dedicated pool. They want a tested, low-risk policy to degrade features (quant profile, batching, KV prefetch) in production without full rollback to prior model version. Impact: Customer-facing chat experiences intermittent timeouts and elevated token costs due to retries. Request: concrete step-by-step safe-degradation policy and one-line CLI/API commands for toggles, plus verification checklist and recommended monitoring thresholds.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer enabled rw-13b-quant-v2 quant profile (q8_0) via model config on Dedicated pool
2) Set max_batch_size=2048 and enabled kv_prefetch=true in optimizer config
3) Observed increased request latencies and occasional streaming broken pipes under steady load (~120 rps)
4) Reproduce under prod-like traffic using loadgen: mean seq_len=512, 30% streaming responses
logs: 2026-03-13T10:12:43Z WARN serving-runtime: kv-prefetch eviction miss spike (rate 18.6%)
2026-03-13T10:13:01Z ERROR gateway: downstream stream disconnected code=ABORTED trace=abc123
investigation_notes: Support triage: symptoms align with aggressive batch sizes + quant profile edge-case kernel path that increases assembly latency for long sequences.
SRE checked Dedicated pool GPU utilization: per-GPU occupancy ~88% with spikes to 96% concurrently with latency spikes.
KV-prefetch shows higher miss ratio after enabling new quant profile — hypothesis: memory layout change increased kv cache fragmentation leading to extra CPU work.
No code regressions found in serving-runtime in last 72h; related PR touched kernel selection heuristics (see PR #4123) — flagged for engineering review.

Immediate risk: full rollback to previous model version will reduce throughput predictability and requires a pinned version change in customer configs; customer prefers staged degradations instead of full revert.
mitigation_workaround: Apply staged feature degradations in order of lowest customer-visible regression to highest. Recommended immediate safe sequence: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 512, 2) disable kv_prefetch, 3) apply quant profile reduced aggressiveness (q8_1 -> q8_2 or switch to q16 fallback), 4) if still unstable, fallback route to gpt-4o-mini-compat for a subset of traffic via routing policy. Each step should be applied as a canary to 5-10% traffic with 10 minute observation windows.
rollback_runbook_steps: Step A - Canary reduce batch: API PATCH /v1/configs/{pool} set optimizer.max_batch_size=512; verify p95 latency and batch assembly delay for 10 minutes
Step B - Toggle kv_prefetch: API PATCH /v1/configs/{pool} set optimizer.kv_prefetch=false; watch kv miss rate, CPU steal, and stream disconnect metrics for 15 minutes
Step C - De-escalate quant profile: API PATCH /v1/models/{model}/profile set profile=q8_2 or set profile_fallback_to=q16; confirm model correctness tests against golden prompts
Step D - Route fallback: Create routing rule to send 10% traffic to gpt-4o-mini-compat via Console -> Routing -> Add Rule; monitor error budget and token cost delta

Step E - If regressions persist after Steps A-D, perform model version revert: PATCH /v1/models/{customer_model}/pin set version={previous-stable}; coordinate a 5-minute maintenance window and notify customer
